evidence: Conditional competitive-cost and industrial-capacity scenarios. All process qualification, future costs, orders, power, reserves and capital funding are assumed. No lunar cost advantage is inferred from the physical calculation.

boundaries: Factories are assumed qualified and already commissioned. No opportunity to build or expand them is adopted; loss cases show why a plant should not be built without orders.
Output is limited by shared nameplate, utilization, yield, energy, explicit annual buyer budgets and orders, remaining buyer stock allocations and a finite local-feed allowance.
Equal-technology costs are assumptions. A lower-price lunar offer requires delivered cost below both Earth and array alternatives; identical quality and performance are assumed.
Capital is inferred from a declared capital-service fraction of benchmark unit cost at normal saleable utilization. This is an economic allowance, not an equipment bill.

Initial capital is half equity/sponsor and half debt. Replacement cash reserves, debt service and fixed operating costs remain payable when demand is weak. Required equity dividends and full settlement costs remain unpriced.

Array programme sales create real production but do not independently finance the combined Moon-array project. Independent cash is allocated proportionally to independently funded receipts, not added to earlier income scenarios.
All output here is sold and delivered during the operating window. Separate stockpile cases use their own purchase budgets and are alternatives to selling the same goods immediately.
Closure releases unused replacement reserves and assumed salvage, and settles remaining debt. Salvage, debt repayment and asset sales are not current manufacturing GDP.

The three product families share physical market allocations and plant resources. Existing ordinary capital, early-factory activity, mining and construction procurement cannot be summed with these rows without removing overlaps.

Route-throughput limits are explicit capacity assumptions, not demonstrated launch/capture designs. The manufacturing electricity requirement excludes delivery-system energy; all-in freight tariffs include its cost.

Cost competitiveness uses normal saleable utilization; idle capital can make actual project NPV negative even when its offer beats competitors. Assigned operating cash is before a required equity dividend and is not a net gain after initial equity.
The independent-buyer-priority variant trades some private margin for externally funded receipts; it retains the same finite customer budgets and orders.
